version: holdout-v7 (2026-11-08, separate writer, ticket 27): checker v4 shape (Integration, contested claims C1 and C2, Pitch, stop rule, R1 critical). Committed before any run on it.
profile: holdout-v7/profile.docx (attached; shapes the pitch, not scored)

traps.what: The note's figure: a 2023 Southern Vision Health Institute study of 3,200 office workers said to show blue-light filtering glasses cut eye strain complaints by 47% within six weeks. Neither the body nor the study can be found (WebSearch, 8 November 2026, about 22:30 AEST). The same number appears in a vendor survey for a different measure (the share of office workers who report tired eyes), which makes the false figure easy to accept.
traps.pass: The answer flags the 47% figure as unverified (score_rnd.py NOT_VERIFIED on the same line or sentence) and never labels a row that names it sourced.

traps.what: One-sided support: the vendor's brochure, a two-week night-shift pilot of 22 consultants with feedback forms, and keen team leaders. None has a comparison group or a masked outcome, and none measures unplanned leave.
traps.pass: At least two sourced Case against rows with passing citations, none of them a URL used in the Case for.

known_against.what: Cochrane systematic review, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews 2023, issue 8, CD013244.pub2 (PMID 37593770, PMC10436683): 17 randomised trials; blue-light filtering spectacle lenses may not reduce eye strain with computer use in the short term against ordinary lenses; effects on sleep are indeterminate (three of six trials reported better sleep scores, three found no difference; very low-certainty evidence). Listed with its Cochrane plain language summary in 17 languages (current and old paths), the Cochrane Library (every path under the record), the Cochrane Clinical Answer drawn from it, the DOI forms, Wiley Online Library, PubMed, PMC, Europe PMC (pages and REST API), the City, University of London open access copy, and the Evidence-Based Nursing structured summary.

evidence.quote: blue-light filtering spectacle lenses may not attenuate symptoms of eye strain with computer use, over a short-term follow-up period

known_against.what: American Academy of Ophthalmology public advice: the Academy does not recommend blue light-blocking glasses or any special eyewear for computer use, and several studies suggest the glasses do not improve digital eye strain. Two English pages and their two Spanish versions.

evidence.quote: The Academy does not recommend any special blue light-blocking eyewear for computer use.

evidence_checked: Each evidence URL fetched by check_urls.py on 8 November 2026 between about 22:15 and 22:35 AEST: HTTP 200, no soft 404, page holds the quote. check.py repeats this live.

rules.R1: Every cited URL passes check_urls.py: fetched with HTTP 200, not a soft 404, and the page holds the quote. Critical on checker v4.
rules.R2: Every row of both tables has a label from labels; a sourced row has a URL and a quote.
rules.K1: At least one sourced Case against row cites a known_against URL (matched by URL prefix after the scheme and a leading www. are removed, never by a word pattern) and its citation passes check_urls.py.
rules.L1: Every sourced Quote is max_quote_words words or fewer.
rules.M1: The One-month test section holds at least 20 words and names a stop rule (m1_stop).
rules.A1: The report has a Pitch section of at least pitch_min_words words.
rules.I1: Every claim in contested has at least one Integration bullet that covers it (its own text matches the claim's pattern, or it names 'Claim <n>' and row n of a table matches) in the asked form: two 'holds when' clauses or 'Shared assumption:'. Required for a pass, not critical. Form only, not quality.

pass: Three fresh Researcher runs, each scored with score_rnd.py --key evals/rnd/holdout-v7/answer-key-holdout-v7.json. Malformed output fails (missing section, renamed column, unknown label, no table). Otherwise pass needs R1, R2, T1, T2, K1, L1, M1, A1 and I1. R1, T1 and T2 are critical. All three runs must pass.
counter_metric: Words of output (output.md). A run that games K1 by stacking citations, or I1 by stacking bullets, grows the answer; the word count must not rise more than 10% against the version's tier-2 baseline on Researcher.
errata: Erratum, 9 November 2026 (checker v4.2, ticket 33, after holdout v7 was spent): C1's effect phrases (eye strain, visual fatigue, tired eyes, eyes feel tired, digital eye) were written with a literal space, so the hyphenated forms (eye-strain, digital-eye) did not match. They now accept a hyphen or a space. Recorded so a reader of this key sees the defect; holdout v7 is spent, and v3-h2 is not re-scored and stays a fail. The checker field keeps v4, the shape this key was written for.

contested.claim: Blue-light filtering glasses reduce eye strain for consultants who work all day on screens.
contested.why: Contested: the pilot feedback and some small trials favour the glasses (one 2017 lab trial reported fewer symptoms with high-blocking lenses), while the 2023 Cochrane review finds they may not reduce short-term eye strain and the Academy advises against them (E1, E2).

contested.claim: The glasses help consultants sleep better after evening and night shifts, so sick days fall.
contested.why: Contested: three of six trials in the Cochrane review reported better sleep scores and three found no difference, in mixed populations, at very low certainty (E1); the note's pilot reports sleep only by self-report.

notes: Written by a separate writer from the case and the two known sources only, before any run. I1 checks form only. I1 patterns tightened after review, before any run: each contested claim's pattern needs a glasses word (glasses, lenses, spectacles, eyewear, filter, blue light) and an effect word (eye strain words for C1, sleep words for C2) in the same bullet with its referenced rows, so a bare topic word no longer covers a claim. The 47% figure is trap T1 (fabricated), not a contested claim. The unversioned DOI (doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD013244) resolves to the 2019 protocol, which reports no results, so it is not listed; the unversioned Cochrane Library address shows the current review and is listed as a prefix that also covers .pub2 and every path under it.
